item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports combining item text with collaborative IDs, but provides limited direct evidence for a GRU model whose text encoder is trained entirely from scratch. [TedRec (CIKM 2024)](https://github.com/RUCAIBox/TedRec) integrates text and ID representations through sequence-level fusion; its experiments use pretrained BERT features and a SASRec backbone. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) uses BERT representations of titles, descriptions and reviews, motivating text as a way to distinguish items and alleviate sparsity. Neither establishes that these gains transfer to the constrained, title-and-description-only GRU setting. [WhitenRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10602) identifies another concern: overly similar text embeddings can impair item discrimination.\n\nA task-compatible hypothesis is to retain GRU4Rec and jointly train a small token-embedding encoder with mean pooling or a CNN over supplied titles/descriptions. Fuse its projected output with item-ID embeddings inside one network, and use the same learned item representation for history encoding and candidate scoring. Shared tokens could transfer supervision to sparse items, while IDs preserve distinctions between similarly described products; this is an inference, not a demonstrated result from the cited studies. Compare against the corrected ID-only baseline using fixed macro validation HR@10, with training-frequency slices as diagnostics. Inspect missing text and representation similarity before adding complexity. Product purpose, entertainment style and simulator explanations remain hypotheses rather than observed intent labels; use no pretrained weights, unavailable reviews, independent predictors or score fusion."}
